Well peeps, this short video may help you as it has opened my mind eyes: I used to be a perfectionist, but little did i know that I was more of a procrastinator than a perfectionist. Every business has business plan. So is trading. Here are some examples I pulled up: * Omidfx: readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...club?start=175#56499 * Edge: readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...es-journal-2-0#61591 * Michal238 : readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...-s-journal-2-0#60739 RTM should have one, but where is it? It's all in price reading article. Thanks also to our RTM founders, we are now guided by Markepedia Roadmap & the "FAQ" article. Based on all these, we still need to make our own "TRADING" business plan, dont we? well, how about developing the price reading article to include markepedia roadmap. Now, our price reading article becomes longer than half a page long, but more detailed and has psychology & money management aspects too. Remember though: the plan is still very much gravitated towards PAR rule of thumb. Then, based on our findings from our trades, screentime, homeworks; we can always add/remove/update the price reading article. What's more interesting is to add IF's bits & pieces of lessons to it, just to add some flavors. In addition to that, how about adding IF's quotes complied by Deenius: readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...-war?start=750#56612 Now our business plan starts looking like a manual, doesnt it? Please be careful not to make it too mechanical. Market is manipulated. Profits are not exactly profits, neither are losses. It is all about transfer of wealth from the manipulated to the manipulator. So the manual just helps us to understand price structures. How the ITs profit from price moves is another side of the balance we need to interpret for ourselves. Having both mechanical & psychological sides balanced, we should be more sensitive towards "what may/will happen". Having said that, every single one of us will have different business plan, hence different practice and different trading style. no one is ever the same. Yes, we all will look similar and often take same trades, but the process inside of us will never be exactly similar. Let us not search for perfection, because perfection risks us to be a procrastinator and focus too much on the results we desperately need to achieve (just like the youtube video said); but instead, start building the pieces slowly and patiently, enjoy the process, and what is much more important, just like IF said: "feel more at home" with the charts. Bro PinkPanter, i hope this post helps you and everyone in answering what you look for. Best wishes, S Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Most SD traders still look directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading. It's further left again we should be looking. Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely simple stuff. We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Gold digging 30 Mar 2018 14:43 #453 staurum Topic Author --> Offline Master Trader Posts: 940 Thank you received: 1954 Just wanna share a little perspective on this holiday time, in which i got a chance to revisit our education home. To those who have run so far but feel that we've hit a giant unsolvable wall in a maze. Maybe it's a good idea to start a chart with basic Supply & Demand brain. Do we remember that RTM all initiated there? (from HTF to lower TFs as many as we wish). Initially we would trade the S/D zones blindly, right? let's move on. Markepedia says: " The truth is; supply/demand are often reactions to the Flag Limit (a RBD or DBR after a break of a high or low) ". This is all we need to know, the rest would be personal homework. We can ask yourself a whole bunch of questions, but structure our questions like we would structure a maze. For example: "That zone simply looks like a supply/demand zone, but is it really? is it a reaction or a break just before retrace?" "let's say it's a reaction, then which flag limit that zone reacts to?.... hang on, a flag limit was initially just an FTR that met its target, let us look to the left and see where/whatzone that flag limit seeks to target?.... mm... which zone that flag limit fails to return to? and in that zone, is there clean orders? that could be the target of a break of this flag limit?" "now looking at the target of that flag limit, where was this target actually targeting towards? (remember that the target of an engulf is just an opposite engulf? - this would bring us further into some loops/series of questions again... so this would be the expansion of the maze) " "ok, let's go back, if this supply/demand is a reaction, has the reaction reached its target? if not yet, then we might have a trade opp. if not, then no good opp, but is there an unfilled orders in the zone it is reaction to? if so, what would we do?" "Let's say it's a break of a zone to the left, then we would not try to look to trade this zone, but where is the next zone that this break is targeting towards? If this is a break, where price *should return to*, and where are the clean orders that may ping-pong price to reach its tg." let's go back and re-ask: "ok this supply/demand zone does not look like a reaction, nor a break - seems to happen in the middle of nowhere." or "mm... this supply/demand zone looks like a break of this zone but a reaction of that zone"... this would bring us into another size of maze of questions. Also, maybe we can ask something like "ok where was price departing from before reaching this supply/demand zone? is that departure zone a reaction or a break?" and so on and so on. Do we remember a saying "price travels from supply to demand and vice versa"? well here in RTM we are trying to be that Supply/Demand or Spike low/high. Just remember the origins of our thought process, because we will very easily lose ourselves into solving some branch areas of the maze but forgot the structure of the original maze we were coming from. To me, personally, RTM is not a puzzle. Puzzle is limited, but i dont think a knowledge is limited. Instead, i personally "feel", RTM is a growing maze of knowledge. RTM creates the centre of it and it is up to us to "expand our map of understanding price action". RTM gives us a starting platform of thought for our own journey to understand the market. RTM is not a destination whereby all knowledge is complete and finished already. It truly is not. We may feel stuck or getting nowhere, but we need to ask ourselves if it is because RTM stops guiding us into the further dark zone of the maze, or maybe if it is because we are just too afraid to expand ourselves more due to fear of being wrong or fear of getting lost. This sort of process, in my opinion, can't be literally orchestrated in a forum, let alone in an open group chat (otherwise, RTM will turn into tradingview.com forums, where the blinds are leading the deafs but they are all quacking each other to exhaustion). Trading is very much correlated to working on ourselves. Each individual of us has different brain and therefore different maze of thoughts. We would be "typically similar" but will never be the same with each other. May we all have a good, enjoyable rest time in this short holiday. on a side note, remember that the celebration of this holiday originates from some very evil events. The blankets are so divine and holy, but most humans are naively lured into unconsciously, by default, celebrating the things very undeserving. Am i prepared? -Where is the MPL on this scale? -Am i the " Patsy" retailer? Or the astute IT like trader? -Does it makes sense on HTF? -Does it makes sense on LTF? -Where is price coming from? -How is it approaching my zone?Breaking a flag?Broken other FL i have ignored?Flagged? CP? Pole? -Is there evidence of IT activity? -What are the IT doing at my level ? Loading? Unloading? F$#@ing retailers out of their money? -Where is the next zone of interest (ignored FL/Engulfed FL ) -Is TG 1 far away enough to make this worth while? Of course don't miss the most important article on trading i have ever read it has the best set of questions : www.readthemarket.com/index.php/price-reading I'm not taking credit for them as i have found them studying some of the greatest journals i could find here on RTM....so feel free to use them, share them and add some more to the list . Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Gold digging 21 Mar 2017 19:51 #103 staurum Topic Author --> Offline Master Trader Posts: 940 Thank you received: 1954 Price is Fractal I have poured a lot of thoughts, maybe too much that i ended up falling asleep as i read and watched about it. lol A couple of good videos that i like: I currently follow Mandelbrot: "Fractal" is such a fascinating subject. I thought fractal is all about structures, order, similar shapes. Instead, fractal is beyond that. It also encompasses chaos and unstructured roughness. Many science has applied fractal concept into explaining mother nature and modern science. I wont be the one explaining. Life, age, time and space, all is indeed fractal. From what i understand, Fractal has size, scaling factor and dimension. A line has 1 dimension. A plain has 2 dimension. A box is 3-D. Sierpinski mesh is 1.585-D. Britain's coastline dimension can be calculated. Even any island's coastline can be calculated. How can something so unorderly, chaotic, unstructured be considered fractal? well sea surface is, just as much as the clouds in the sky. One characteristic of fractal is a small part of it looks/represents/mimics the whole of it. So as we zoom in to these matters, as small/little/tiny as they can be, they look/represent/mimic the whole of them. Why is dimension needed? it has something to do with scaling factor. but, what about price chart? I dont have the answer, but somehow my mind goes to ( readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...gging?start=75#61669 ) and what charvo said " let's imagine price is drawing a tree, price has to firstly draw the trunk, then the branches, finally the leaves. on the other hand, when the tree dies, the leaves fall first, then branch broken down, and finally the trunk collapse. there's a fixed order. when you scrutinize a piece of a branch, you see the same order; when you oversee a forest, it still follow the same order...... and relate these with timeframe, that probably helps on topic of 'scale' ." What is a trunk to some branches could be just one of the branches to a bigger trunk. The opposite could also be true: what is a branch to a trunk could be the trunk for other branches and also some leaves. It really depends on when and where the piece is located. [Funnily, RTM teaching goes the same. In that, who is now a teacher to some students could have been once a student among others to another teacher. In turn, who is now a student may well be a teacher for some other students. It really depends on when and where the person is currently. That is how market is best studied] Also, it is assumed that the tree stops growing for some reason or is already fully grown. It may be another different story if we know that the tree is still growing. It will also be another different story if we know that the tree is collapsing. Why need to know if the tree is growing/collapsing? Because the scaling factor will matter and we can better identify the positioning of a piece inside the tree if we know the full story/picture of the tree. I just dont know yet how to turn this fully into charts/price. After marking and drawing some charts into a set of messy print-outs (after which my kids turned perfectly into a chaotic paper toss game), I realised that a flag can turn into a flag limit in a higher scale; a pole in a scale is just a small PAZ inside a flag; poles and flags stacked in one direction makes a higher scale pole; poles and flags zoned against each other makes a higher scale flag. As Sali often repeated to me, price moves from FL to FL. Of course he cant tell me in what scale, but he already directs me into the direction, i.e. deeper study of FL which is the chain-link of everything else. Again, my curiosity goes back to " Investigate flag completion and evaluate how price can move in order to complete a yet to be completed flag " 7:45pm: late dinner already Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Gold digging 11 Apr 2017 00:21 #117 staurum Topic Author --> Offline Master Trader Posts: 940 Thank you received: 1954 Hi Frosty, Having an emergency in singapore. just got a chance to open up a laptop and back to the markets. so ok, EG: Of all scales and timeframes, we need to go to the highest. so yes, weekly is great. but timeframe doesnot matter, what we need is to cover the whole history, so you need to zoom out the timespan as wide as possible. Only after working in the highest/the widest, then we can work down on smaller scales within the limits found. So i just want to focus on the first chart, as the rest just follows through. Now, when you say "significant high", once price breaks that high, price made a no-return move. So the FTB/2TB/3TB/n-TB is tradable. However, as you noticed already, the this "FTB/2TB/3TB/n-TB" can also be broken back down. now the question is: if this "broken back down" happens; where is the target anyway? This will answer a question if you are asked "why is a level you say/consider "significant high" is indeed significant. People look for a bounce or entry at the left shoulder levels, but often times have totally forgotten all the other important stuffs that are necessary for us to RTM. I do hope you notice what i mean here. Another is, (my mistake that i dont want anybody to follow), only mark a zone/level according to what happens on its left, not according to what happens to its right. By this, i mean for every turn, i was trying to understand what FTR the turn is reacting to, and mark that FTR as FL. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Gold digging 19 Jul 2017 10:05 #197 staurum Topic Author --> Offline Master Trader Posts: 940 Thank you received: 1954 I think this is a great reminder for everybody who's lost in price reading. In his webinar, IF literally defines: "how do you differentiate a fake engulf and a real engulf?" "A fake engulf is just a BREAK of a LOW or an High, which hasNOT broken what they are actually a reaction to." Some of the mistakes I made, as follows: * treating an entry like an exit or vice versa . It is generally true that we entry as if we're ready to exit from an opposite position as if we have one, and vice versa: we exit as if we're ready to entry for the next opposite swing. What is different though: an open position will have several targets but one stoploss. in other words, an open position will have several "happy exits" but one "suck toilet flush". on the contrary, It is definitely not correct for an open position to have one target but several stoplosses, in otherwords one "happy exit" but several "toilet flush" points - this just does not work in trading. what i simply mean here, a profitable position, when closed, does NOT necessarily then interpret an entry for the opposite direction. This i think, is just to satisfy our ego "to be correct" and our greed "to get rich quick", oh and one more --> i need to be trading so i need to click, click, click - entry, entry, entry. This will happen a lot when there are so many temptations (even to an expression of "seductions", i feel) when looking in LTF, for example 1m chart. * watching approach and reaction. We need to be really really careful when zoning our approaching flags and determining which is reaction and which is non-reaction yet. When price is going up towards our interest zone (flag limit zone at an important barrier), we mark the flags price prints as it upwardly breaks the LTF barriers - this is what we call watching the approach. Only after price has hit our interest zone, we need to see whether one or more of the approaching flags we mark on LTF is engulfed, which then allows us to even consider an entry, or not. same in the opposite direction: when price is going down towards our interest zone, we mark the flags price prints as it downwardly breaks the LTF barriers. and only after the zone is hit, we need to see one or more of the approaching flags is engulfed to consider an entry, or not. Well, we need to be careful though, because it may not be as simple as that. These maybe related to "curve fitting": - determining which zone, be it a whole flag or a miniflag inside it, that needs to be engulfed, to allow us to consider an entry; will be so obvious at times, but many times can be a little bit tricky. - even after we find an engulf, our entry will sometimes be lost for many reasons. this is when our "psychology" requires discipline. - our interest zone "can be" broken and then price makes a giant retrace to the point of us thinking whether or not our zoning/analysis is correct, let alone trade-able. again, this would be when our psychology is being tested. we need to understand price is all about manipulation. in order for price to move beyond, it needs to do the breaks and also selfdoubts + confusions. - another one, when price is going up towards our interest zone, we need to "carefully & critically" assess, whether or not the engulf (thus decision of direction) has already happened in one higher timescale up, therefore this upmove is "merely" a retrace back ( not an approaching move ) to some unpicked orders. In some occasions, our interest zone "may" be inside a bigger "interest zone" OR in "FRONT" of the "more important zone", and therefore whether or not there is good approach and/or good reaction, price may fake-out beyond our initial interest zone, thus we mistakenly conclude it as an engulf, but then price shoots down even beyond our target had we been able to trade it based on our initial analysis, or maybe after we conclude it as an engulf, we're ready to take an entry at the zone where we thought to be "origin of the move" and price shoots past it, we are left confused. Same applies for "when price is going down". - last but not least (i might add some more): patience is truly a virtue, knowing when not to trade is just as important as when to trade. nonetheless, neither is more important than self-mindmastery & discipline Trading left & right, ups & downs is truly beautiful, but i find that most often price just needs to structure itself out just for us to take the profit out of it. Most people call it the set-ups. But it's just what price gives us. It structures itself, leave some unpicked orders for us, dances around, and then we need to "be sensitive" to its clue of invites (or traps). Trying to trade when price hasnot finished its structures is kinda similar to trying to taste some food in the kitchen that a chef hasnot finished preparing. If we're as professional in food, then we know what the finish-up should taste like, but the trouble comes when we are arrogant and act as if we're more qualified to prepare the food and then starts making interventions. I wish i can write this simpler. anyone is very much welcome to contributing. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Gold digging #453 staurum Offline Master Trader Posts: 1002 Thank you received: 2144 Just wanna share a little perspective on this holiday time, in which i got a chance to revisit our education home. To those who have run so far but feel that we've hit a giant unsolvable wall in a maze. Maybe it's a good idea to start a chart with basic Supply & Demand brain. Do we remember that RTM all initiated there? (from HTF to lower TFs as many as we wish). https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=450 3/39 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 19 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Initially we would trade the S/D zones blindly, right? let's move on. Markepedia says: "The truth is; supply/demand are often reactions to the Flag Limit (a RBD or DBR after a break of a high or low)". This is all we need to know, the rest would be personal homework. We can ask yourself a whole bunch of questions, but structure our questions like we would structure a maze. For example: "That zone simply looks like a supply/demand zone, but is it really? is it a reaction or a break just before retrace?" https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=450 4/39 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 19 - RTM Community "let's say it's a reaction, then which flag limit that zone reacts to?.... hang on, a flag limit HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT was initially just an FTR that met its target, let us look to the left and see where/whatzone that flag limit seeks to target?.... mm... which zone that flag limit fails to return to? and in that zone, is there clean orders? that could be the target of a break of this flag limit?" "now looking at the target of that flag limit, where was this target actually targeting towards? (remember that the target of an engulf is just an opposite engulf? - this would bring us further into some loops/series of questions again... so this would be the expansion of the maze) " "ok, let's go back, if this supply/demand is a reaction, has the reaction reached its target? if not yet, then we might have a trade opp. if not, then no good opp, but is there an unfilled orders in the zone it is reaction to? if so, what would we do?" "Let's say it's a break of a zone to the left, then we would not try to look to trade this zone, but where is the next zone that this break is targeting towards? If this is a break, where price *should return to*, and where are the clean orders that may ping-pong price to reach its tg." let's go back and re-ask: "ok this supply/demand zone does not look like a reaction, nor a break - seems to happen in the middle of nowhere." or "mm... this supply/demand zone looks like a break of this zone but a reaction of that zone"... this would bring us into another size of maze of questions. Also, maybe we can ask something like "ok where was price departing from before reaching this supply/demand zone? is that departure zone a reaction or a break?" and so on and so on. Do we remember a saying "price travels from supply to demand and vice versa"? well here in RTM we are trying to be that Supply/Demand or Spike low/high. Just remember the origins of our thought process, because we will very easily lose ourselves into solving some branch areas of the maze but forgot the structure of the original maze we were coming from. To me, personally, RTM is not a puzzle. Puzzle is limited, but i dont think a knowledge is limited. Instead, i personally "feel", RTM is a growing maze of knowledge. RTM creates the centre of it and it is up to us to "expand our map of understanding price action". RTM gives us a starting platform of thought for our own journey to understand the market. RTM is not a destination whereby all knowledge is complete and finished already. It truly is not. We may feel stuck or getting nowhere, but we need to ask https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=450 5/39 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 19 - RTM Community ourselves if it is because RTM stops guiding us into the further dark zone of the maze, HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT or maybe if it is because we are just too afraid to expand ourselves more due to fear of being wrong or fear of getting lost. This sort of process, in my opinion, can't be literally orchestrated in a forum, let alone in an open group chat (otherwise, RTM will turn into tradingview.com forums, where the blinds are leading the deafs but they are all quacking each other to exhaustion). Trading is very much correlated to working on ourselves. Each individual of us has different brain and therefore different maze of thoughts. We would be "typically similar" but will never be the same with each other. May we all have a good, enjoyable rest time in this short holiday. on a side note, remember that the celebration of this holiday originates from some very evil events. The blankets are so divine and holy, but most humans are naively lured into unconsciously, by default, celebrating the things very undeserving. Let's get on with it. It's quite a common sense, generally publicly accepted, that price moves because of orders executed. This is a necessary and sufficient premise. If price moves because of some sort of magic hand, holy grail patterns, dark secret indicators or even a ghost, it *could be* a necessary premise, but how sufficient it is to be true rises too many works to deduce. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=450 8/39 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 19 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Orders, the culprit, to be executed are none other than limit orders, stop orders, and market orders, regardless of them being entries or exits. Of course, there will be combinations like OCOs, etc, but I deem them unnecessary. Another necessary & sufficient premise is that price moves (ups or downs) because one-sided orders overpower/overconsume the other-sided orders. My, doubtful, assumptions are that: While no matter how hard players try their best to hide their cards, the house always know, but the house itself will always hide their hands. The players can not and will not beat the house. The house may passively let the players to win from time to time, or actively catch the bets (the orders) by overpowering the players. Shifting it a little into vocabulary of orders: The house never leaves resting orders, i.e. limit orders and stop orders, to be seen by everybody else. Therefore, it is likely that the players leave the resting orders, although it is also possible for them to execute at-market orders, it is common sense that the house (the one having hidden their hands) moves price by executing its at-market orders against the opposite orders. Thinking about orders: Limit orders cannot exist without stop(loss) orders. Stop(entry) orders, however, do not need limit orders, but will likely have its own stop(loss) orders too. Limit orders are commonly placed in front of a H/L of some sort, and therefore stops behind that H/L. It is my own guess that these limit orders belong to S&D players, S/R players, or perhaps Trendline players. Stop(entry) orders are usually placed beyond (or, on a break) of a H/L of some sort, and usually stops behind the opposite L/H. Again, it is my own guess that these stops belong to Break-Out players, or trend-following players. The volume of orders on execution at a level at any given time, will decide the move and also the extent of the move. Search "order flow" or "market auction theory" on youtube. plenty of examples. basics of supply & demand concept. The volume of orders ultimately depend upon the decision AND the capacity (or capital/investment limit) of the *betters*. It is always the house's choice, depending on its own interest and intent, to either let the resting orders to be executed without intervention (i call it "pass the bet" https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=450 9/39 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 19 - RTM Community on purpose), HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT or catch the resting orders by executing its at-market orders (i call it "call the bet") to fill its book. One thing I absolutely believe is that the house *survives* by feeding off *Large Sums of Orders*, and it never loses to the players. In regards to H/L: this is very subjective concept. In a very simple way: A Level is considered a High, if price travels from it to break the previous relative lows. Vice versa, A Level is considered a Low, if price travels from it to break the previous relative highs. How do we classify them? I personally think that the more important question is how do we compare their *sexiness*? Well, perhaps the more distant the H/L travels from its previous L/H before the break, the more attractive and the more obvious it is to the players (but not necessarily the house). Obvious H/L levels are commonly basis levels from which the players (S&D traders, BreakOut traders, Trendline traders, Fibo-ers, Indicator traders, Wave traders, etc.) analyse the charts and place their trades. It is my wild, unconfirmed guess that the more obvious it is, the more attractive the sum of orders are to be executed "around" there. In order for H/L to exist, there must be reversals and breaks. The reasons behind the reversals and the breaks are still homeworks. How are they related to each other? No idea yet. How do we take advantage in the trading? Still in progress. Is the market driven by emotions (fear & greed)? It maybe necessary, but when and where it is a sufficient premise, remains work in progress. On another dimension of talk: It is my own adopted-from-rtm personal belief that the ITs work their way down from HTF to LTF. hence, my own wild guess is: a winner in lower scale can be a loser in a higher scale, but a winner in a higher scale will always be a winner on a lower scale. a loser in lower scale will always be a loser in higher scale, though a loser in higher scale can be a winner in lower scale. I could be very wrong in any, some, or the whole of these writings. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Gold digging #465 fxeyes Away Trader Posts: 176 Thank you received: 98 I always try think of things in ways that makes logical sense. With an engulf, I imagine that the ITs or whoever knows there's large orders somewhere (FLs, S/R), and they'll push orders until that breaks. Because once its broken, now they know there isn't anything major against them and they can easily get to their next target. From there they can manipulate price between the major sets of orders (FLs) and get their fill because other's nothing in-between to stop them. If they don't do that, they won't know how many orders are against them, and they'll be taking a major risk without testing that level first. And they just keep doing this until they hit their final target. Anyways, i dont know if that's actually true or not, but that type of thinking helps me explain why engulfs are so powerful. That the greatest aim of life is Eudemonia. This is a Greek term that means happiness or living the good life - careful, don't confuse it with pleasure or success - for them is living a contemplative life and embodying the truth and living from Good. Philosophy is about what is true. Pyrrhonism says that nothing can be known for certain because you have two ways of accessing reality. The first one is the senses and the other one is reasoning. The problem is that they are not reliable and can trick us very easily. Therefore, we have to be honest and admit that we cannot know reality for sure. Neither perceptions nor reasoning tell us the ultimate truth. Moreover, he taught us that reasoning or proof is either, circular, https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=550 2/43 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 23 - RTM Community or involves an infinite regress that is ultimately groundless. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT How do we usually know what is true? We claim something and then back it up with justifications and proofs and evidence, but if we really think about it this is groundless because for any evidence you provide, you will need more evidence to prove itself and so on. You cannot basically ground anything because you don't any grounding proof. You cannot say something is true because with each statement, its contradiction may be advanced with equal justification. THEREFORE, PYRRHONISTS REFUSE TO TAKE ANY POSITIONS BECAUSE WE DON'T HAVE GROUNDS FOR TAKING IT. THEY REFUSE TO TAKE SIDES. They will doubt anything beyond appearances because they cannot be ultimately proven. They also oppose that nothing can be known. The problem with the modern skeptic is that they doubt their own skepticism. You cannot know if nothing can be known. To make that sort of claim would be dogmatic. "Skepticism is an ability or mental attitude with opposes judgement in any way whatsoever, with the results that, we are brought to a state of mental suspense, and then to a state of quietude. Suspense is a state of mental rest in which we don't deny or affirm anything. Quietude is a tranquil condition of the soul. The main basic principle of the skeptic system is that of opposing to every proposition, an opposite proposition for we believe that as a consequence o this, we end to seizing to dogmatize." Many science has applied fractal concept into explaining mother nature and modern science. I wont be the one explaining. Life, age, time and space, all is indeed fractal. From what i understand, Fractal has size, scaling factor and dimension. A line has 1 dimension. A plain has 2 dimension. A box is 3-D. Sierpinski mesh is 1.585-D. Britain's coastline dimension can be calculated. Even any island's coastline can be calculated. How can something so unorderly, chaotic, unstructured be considered fractal? well sea surface is, just as much as the clouds in the sky. One characteristic of fractal is a small part of it looks/represents/mimics the whole of it. So as we zoom in to these matters, as small/little/tiny as they can be, they look/represent/mimic the whole of them. Why is dimension needed? it has something to do with scaling factor. but, what about price chart? What is a trunk to some branches could be just one of the branches to a bigger trunk. The opposite could also be true: what is a branch to a trunk could be the trunk for other branches and also some leaves. It really depends on when and where the piece is located. [Funnily, RTM teaching goes the same. In that, who is now a teacher to some students could have been once a student among others to another teacher. In turn, who is now a student may well be a teacher for some other students. It really depends on when and where the person is currently. That is how market is best studied] Also, it is assumed that the tree stops growing for some reason or is already fully grown. It may be another different story if we know that the tree is still growing. It will also be another different story if we know that the tree is collapsing. Why need to know if the tree is growing/collapsing? Because the scaling factor will matter and we can better identify the positioning of a piece inside the tree if we know the full story/picture of the tree. I just dont know yet how to turn this fully into charts/price. The following user(s) said Thank You: staurum QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Gold digging #197 staurum Offline Master Trader Posts: 1002 Thank you received: 2144 I think this is a great reminder for everybody who's lost in price reading. In his webinar, IF literally defines: "how do you differentiate a fake engulf and a real engulf?" "A fake engulf is just a BREAK of a LOW or an High, which hasNOT broken what they are actually a reaction to." Some of the mistakes I made, as follows: * treating an entry like an exit or vice versa. It is generally true that we entry as if we're ready to exit from an opposite position as if we have one, and vice versa: we exit as if we're ready to entry for the next opposite swing. What is different though: an open position will have several targets but one stoploss. in other words, an open position will have several "happy exits" but one "suck toilet flush". on the contrary, It is definitely not correct for an open position to have one target but several stoplosses, in otherwords https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=175 24/30 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 8 - RTM Community one "happy exit" but several "toilet flush" points - this just does not work in trading. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT what i simply mean here, a profitable position, when closed, does NOT necessarily then interpret an entry for the opposite direction. This i think, is just to satisfy our ego "to be correct" and our greed "to get rich quick", oh and one more --> i need to be trading so i need to click, click, click - entry, entry, entry. This will happen a lot when there are so many temptations (even to an expression of "seductions", i feel) when looking in LTF, for example 1m chart. * watching approach and reaction. We need to be really really careful when zoning our approaching flags and determining which is reaction and which is non-reaction yet. When price is going up towards our interest zone (flag limit zone at an important barrier), we mark the flags price prints as it upwardly breaks the LTF barriers - this is what we call watching the approach. Only after price has hit our interest zone, we need to see whether one or more of the approaching flags we mark on LTF is engulfed, which then allows us to even consider an entry, or not. same in the opposite direction: when price is going down towards our interest zone, we mark the flags price prints as it downwardly breaks the LTF barriers. and only after the zone is hit, we need to see one or more of the approaching flags is engulfed to consider an entry, or not. Well, we need to be careful though, because it may not be as simple as that. These maybe related to "curve fitting": - determining which zone, be it a whole flag or a miniflag inside it, that needs to be engulfed, to allow us to consider an entry; will be so obvious at times, but many times can be a little bit tricky. - even after we find an engulf, our entry will sometimes be lost for many reasons. this is when our "psychology" requires discipline. - our interest zone "can be" broken and then price makes a giant retrace to the point of us thinking whether or not our zoning/analysis is correct, let alone trade-able. again, this would be when our psychology is being tested. we need to understand price is all about manipulation. in order for price to move beyond, it needs to do the breaks and also selfdoubts + confusions. - another one, when price is going up towards our interest zone, we need to "carefully & critically" assess, whether or not the engulf (thus decision of direction) has already happened in one higher timescale up, therefore this upmove is "merely" a retrace back (not an approaching move) to some unpicked orders. In some occasions, our interest zone "may" be inside a bigger "interest zone" OR in "FRONT" of the "more important zone", and therefore whether or not there is good approach and/or good reaction, price https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2608-gold-digging?start=175 25/30 7/27/2018 Gold digging - Page 8 - RTM Community may fake-out beyond our initial interest zone, thus we mistakenly conclude it as an HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT engulf, but then price shoots down even beyond our target had we been able to trade it based on our initial analysis, or maybe after we conclude it as an engulf, we're ready to take an entry at the zone where we thought to be "origin of the move" and price shoots past it, we are left confused. Same applies for "when price is going down". - last but not least (i might add some more): patience is truly a virtue, knowing when not to trade is just as important as when to trade. nonetheless, neither is more important than self-mindmastery & discipline Trading left & right, ups & downs is truly beautiful, but i find that most often price just needs to structure itself out just for us to take the profit out of it. Most people call it the set-ups. But it's just what price gives us. It structures itself, leave some unpicked orders for us, dances around, and then we need to "be sensitive" to its clue of invites (or traps). Trying to trade when price hasnot finished its structures is kinda similar to trying to taste some food in the kitchen that a chef hasnot finished preparing. If we're as professional in food, then we know what the finish-up should taste like, but the trouble comes when we are arrogant and act as if we're more qualified to prepare the food and then starts making interventions. I wish i can write this simpler. anyone is very much welcome to contributing. Because making something disappear isn't enough; you have to bring it back. That's why every magic trick has a third act, the hardest part, the part we call "The Prestige"."
